tool.name: pathotypr match
tool.description: finds which reference genome a set of reads is closest to
tool.command:
## The report echoes the input paths back into the first column, so the reads ## are linked to fixed names to keep that column readable and reproducible ## rather than full of Galaxy dataset ids. #if $reads.layout == 'paired' #set $ext = 'fastq.gz' if $reads.pair.forward.is_of_type('fastqsanger.gz') else 'fastq' ln -s '$reads.pair.forward' 'sample_R1.$ext' && ln -s '$reads.pair.reverse' 'sample_R2.$ext' && #else #set $ext = 'fastq.gz' if $reads.single.is_of_type('fastqsanger.gz') else 'fastq' ln -s '$reads.single' 'sample.$ext' && #end if
pathotypr match --references '$references' #if $reads.layout == 'paired' -i 'sample_R1.$ext' 'sample_R2.$ext' --paired #else -i 'sample.$ext' --no-auto-paired #end if --output '$report' --kmer-size $kmer_size --min-kmer-count $min_kmer_count #if float($early_stop_confidence) > 0 --early-stop-confidence $early_stop_confidence --early-stop-min-kmers $early_stop_min_kmers #end if $strict_percentages @THREADS@

param.label: Reference genomes
param.help: A single multi-FASTA holding every candidate reference. Each record is one candidate.

param.label: Minimum k-mer count
param.help: Query k-mers seen fewer times than this are discarded as sequencing noise. Set to 1 to keep singletons. Only applied once the query has more than 100,000 unique k-mers.

param.label: Early-stop confidence
param.help: Stop the exact phase once the leader is this far ahead. 0 disables it and scores everything. Useful values are 0.98 to 0.999.

param.label: Minimum k-mers before early stop
param.help: Ignored unless early-stop confidence is above 0.

param.label: Legacy shared k-mer percentages
param.help: Reproduces the older weighted-count definition of the shared fraction. For comparing against earlier runs.

tool.help:
**What it does**
`pathotypr match` answers one question: of the reference genomes you supply, which one do these reads look most like? It counts how many of the query's k-mers are contained in each reference and reports the best one with the shared fraction behind the call.
Typical uses are picking the closest reference before mapping, and sanity checking that a sample is the species you think it is.
**The output**
============================= ================================================ Column Meaning ============================= ================================================ ``Query_Files`` The read files that went in ``Best_Match_Reference`` The record name of the winning reference ``Shared_Kmer_Fraction`` Fraction of query k-mers contained in it, 0 to 1 ============================= ================================================
A fraction near 1 means the reads are essentially that reference. A low fraction for every candidate means the right reference is not in your set, and the tool will still name a winner, so read the fraction and not only the name.
.. class:: warningmark
**This is the most memory-hungry of the pathotypr tools.** Each batch loads a reference genome and its k-mer set, and both time and memory scale with the number of references multiplied by the number of reads. On a shared Galaxy instance, keep the reference set to the candidates you actually mean to compare, rather than a whole database.
**Early stopping** trades exhaustiveness for speed: once a leader is far enough ahead, the remaining references are not scored exactly. Leave it at 0 when you want the shared fractions of every candidate to be comparable.
